purpose: Matched two-update native fused AdamW continuation comparison: uninterrupted versus checkpoint-interrupted fresh-process execution, with exact model/output/optimizer/schedule/RNG/cursor and resource verification. No convergence or learning-quality claim.

smoke.resume_checkpoint: one full model plus optimizer/RNG/scheduler/cursor checkpoint after update 1
required: checkpoint byte receipt and model/runtime reload
restored scheduler, RNG, optimizer moments and data cursor
resume-start parameter hashes equal the first-process final hashes
all 381 tensors change in each process
native optimizer state step is 2 after resume

required_measurements: per-update forward/backward, gradient audit, clipping and optimizer seconds
warmup and steady update time, updates/s, processed and supervised tokens/s
actual optimizer class, groups, state dtypes and allocated state bytes
sampled driver, process host memory, host free and swap growth

arms.continuous: one fresh native process, two updates, no checkpoint or export
arms.interrupted_first: one fresh native process, update 1 and one retained checkpoint
arms.interrupted_resume: a second fresh native process, update 2 from the first checkpoint

matched_settings: fixed eight-row update plan and supervised-token weighting
seed, warmup, learning rates, gradient norm and nonfinite rejection
global gradient clipping and explicit MPS synchronization
required_comparisons: continuous and resumed final parameter hashes are identical for all 381 tensors
continuous and resumed per-update losses and learning rates are identical
continuous and resumed final fixed-logit SHA256 and loss are identical
resumed optimizer state step is 2 and scheduler/RNG/cursor restoration succeeds
first/resume start hashes and checkpoint receipt validate
all three processes remain within declared resource guards
continuation_comparison.checkpoint_policy: Only interrupted_first writes a checkpoint; continuous and interrupted_resume write no checkpoint or final export
continuation_comparison.raw_policy: Retain every process report, profile, guard log and failure; do not tune against the final comparison

retention.smoke_checkpoint: retain exactly one diagnostic checkpoint for inspection; no promotion and no duplicate final model export
retention.sustained_weights: discard after before/after hashes; preserve only reports/profiles
retention.comparison_weights: no continuous or resume final model export; preserve hashes and output receipts
retention.failures: preserve failure reports, profiles and guard logs
retention.historical_muon: reuse existing three-update evidence; do not rerun Muon

limitations: Short 55-token exposed diagnostic, not a long-context or broad workload benchmark.
The comparison establishes execution/state equivalence only, not convergence, retention or universal speedup.
The fixed-logit receipt is an execution fingerprint, not a generation or task-quality metric.
Sampled memory telemetry can miss transient peaks.
The smoke checkpoint is required only for resume validation and is not a selected model.
